inlines.v: EX'ASPERATE, verb transitive [Latin exaspero, to irritate; ex and aspero, from asper, rough, harsh.] 1. To anger; to irritate to a high degree; to provoke to rage; to enrage; to excite anger, or to inflame it to an extreme degree. We say, to exasperate a person, or to exasperate the passion of anger or resentment. 2. To aggravate; to embitter; as, to exasperate enmity. 3. To augment violence; to increase malignity; to exacerbate; as, to exasperate pain or a part inflamed. EX'ASPERATE, adjective Provoked; embittered; inflamed.
